result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md: waitlist auto-promotion on a freed seat, halting at T-24h. NO SCHEMA CHANGE -- checked apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts directly: registrations already has admission ('waitlisted'/'admitted'), created_at, qr_token, and registrations_waitlist_order_idx (event_id, created_at) WHERE admission='waitlisted'; events already has status/starts_at/ends_at/capacity. DATA-DESIGNER not dispatched for this run.

DESIGN QUESTION 1 (trigger point) RESOLVED: promotion is invoked from WITHIN withdrawRegistration's own transaction (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts, REQ-022 Sec2.2), same tx handle, never a second nested db.transaction -- not a polling job. Matches REQ-022's own stated scope note that the admission column transition IS the seat-freed signal REQ-023 acts on. Gated explicitly: promotion is only attempted when the withdrawn row's pre-withdrawal admission was 'admitted' (captured from withdrawRegistration's existing step-1 read) -- a requested/waitlisted withdrawal frees no seat and skips the call outright.

DESIGN QUESTION 2 (at-most-once) RESOLVED: no new send-marker column. The mechanism is the row's own admission transition -- a waitlisted row can be selected by the promotion candidate query at most once ever (its WHERE admission='waitlisted' filter can never re-select an already-promoted row), and re-running the whole promotion path for the SAME freed seat with no intervening withdrawal finds seatsLeft <= 0 on its own fresh recompute and refuses before ever selecting a row -- so a second run sends nothing because it takes no action, not because a marker suppressed a duplicate. Explicitly flagged as NOT covering a crash between commit and the Telegram send itself (a genuine at-least-once-delivery gap) -- named as REQ-025's future job: key its ledger on (registration_id, notification_kind) and REPLACE this mechanism, not duplicate it.

DESIGN QUESTION 3 (T-24h visibility) RESOLVED: the existing /events command (REQ-017, handlers/event.ts) already surfaces a T-24h-halted freed seat with ZERO new UI -- computeSeatsLeft/buildSeatsLine recompute live from a fresh admitted count on every call, available to any chapter member (organizers included, since /events has no organizer gate). Checked /event_edit's formatEventDump directly too: it shows even less (no admitted count/seats-left at all today). Flagged as an open question that /events' seats-left number alone doesn't distinguish 'never registered' from 'froze at T-24h with a waitlist behind it' -- left for a future (Release 3 manual-promotion) requirement, not invented here.

New pure functions: isAutoPromotionHalted (domain/event.ts, T-24h boundary stated in prose: halted when 24h or less remain before starts_at, eligible when strictly more) and decidePromotionEligibility (domain/registration.ts, ordered table: event-not-eligible (not published OR finished) -> halted-t24h -> capacity-full -> ok). New transactional actor promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible reuses REQ-020's exact FOR UPDATE lock discipline against the events row (same lock order argument proves no over-admission under a concurrent registerForEvent, AC4, and no deadlock since events is the only row both transactions ever contend for) and REQ-021's exact waitlist tie-break (event_id, admission='waitlisted', ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE) to pick the promotion candidate. Writes exactly one audit_log row (actorUserId: null, system-initiated, the writeAuditLog precedent REQ-018's rework already established) on the one write-worthy branch.

WithdrawOutcome's 'withdrawn' member is extended (promotion: PromotionOutcome field added) -- the four refusal members are untouched. Notification is composed and sent in handlers/withdraw.ts's confirm callback, AFTER withdrawRegistration's transaction has committed (matching registration.ts's own established post-commit-display-data pattern), via ctx.api.sendMessage to the PROMOTED person's own tgId (a new domain/user.ts read, getUserForNotificationById, needed since no existing user.ts function resolves tgId/lang starting from an internal users.id) -- flagged as this codebase's first send-to-someone-other-than-ctx.from call site. No broadcast_opt_in check anywhere in that path (S10). Flagged an explicit pre-existing gap (Sec6.4): no QR *delivery* mechanism (image/deep-link) exists anywhere in this codebase yet -- even the direct-registration admitted reply never renders qr_token today -- so this design sends the raw token string as plain text, same fidelity the direct path would have if asked, and recommends ORCH file this as its own issue for a future shared QR-rendering requirement rather than inventing one here.

Every AC mapped to a concrete design element in Sec9's table.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md Sec6.4: no QR *delivery* mechanism (rendered image or scannable deep link) exists anywhere in this codebase today -- confirmed the direct-registration 'admitted' reply (handlers/registration.ts composeRegistrationReply) never renders qr_token either, and checkin.ts's own header comment independently confirms the staff side never reads it. This design satisfies 'notified with their QR' at the same fidelity the direct path already has (raw token string as plain text) rather than inventing QR rendering here. Recommend ORCH file a new issue for a future requirement to give both the direct-admission and promotion paths a single shared ticket/QR-rendering mechanism.

docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md Sec7: /events' live seats-left count satisfies 'visible to the organizer somewhere' as literally required, but does not distinguish a T-24h-halted freed seat (with a non-empty waitlist behind it) from an ordinary never-filled seat. Left as a recommendation for a future (Release 3 manual-promotion) requirement to give organizers a combined seats-left + waitlist-size view, not resolved here since no acceptance criterion in scope asks for new UI.
